rationale: Post-roll review follow-through on council 45b3c93f (Builds-screen backend, APPROVED r1). That round's guardian seat objected that terminate 'relabels the row as terminated/failed without signalling the running process' — the semantics half was answered in the SPA confirm text (commit 1a8db99f9). The review (web_admin_console PLAN_2026-08-24_build_steps_screen.md §7) then found the NUMBER half: correlation_id is NOT unique — measured 2026-08-25, 6,936 orchestration_states rows over 3,102 distinct correlation_ids, up to 19 rows sharing one, and 5 terminate-eligible multi-row correlations live at measurement time — so the terminate UPDATE, scoped only by correlation_id, relabels every sibling and child (including COMPLETED sub-orchestrations) as FAILED with 'Manually terminated by admin', destroying their status record and skewing any consumer that counts FAILED (e.g. agent_handlers.go:475). This was unreachable before e6350e74b fixed the table name (the arm always 500'd against the nonexistent orchestrator_state), so that fix is what armed the blast radius. Second finding, same root: getWorkflowState selects one row by correlation_id with QueryRow and NO ORDER BY, so the admin detail view resolves to an ARBITRARY sibling — a different one on successive opens, with the __step_error panel appearing and disappearing between two clicks on the same row (~40% of correlations are multi-row). Fixes: (1) scope the terminate UPDATE to non-terminal rows — stop what is still running, never rewrite finished work; (2) surface the every-row-already-terminal case as 409 ALREADY_TERMINAL rather than the 500 the RowsAffected==0 path would otherwise produce (the preceding lookup already proved the correlation exists); (3) make getWorkflowState deterministic: root first (parent_orchestration_id IS NULL sorts before NOT NULL), oldest first, LIMIT 1. Tests: new sqlmock file whose expected-SQL regexes ARE the contract (sqlmock matches expectations as regexes against the issued SQL), mutation-proven both ways before submission: deleting the status filter fails TestTerminateScopesToNonTerminalRows (500 on the unmatched exec), deleting the ORDER BY fails the same test via the state-query regex (404 on the unmatched query). A one-line SPA confirm-text correction (frontends/admin-dashboard/src/App.tsx, out of gate scope) rides the same commit: 'marks every still-running orchestration under this correlation FAILED — finished rows are left untouched', replacing the singular 'its state row'. Deliberately NOT changed: no orchestration_id-targeted terminate (a new API surface for a need nobody has stated), no interrupt mechanism (the guardian's semantics point stands — termination remains a DB label), and the resume arm is untouched.

plan.summary: The Builds screen's terminate action, un-broken by e6350e74b, UPDATEs orchestration_states by correlation_id alone — and correlation_id is shared by a parent and its sub-orchestrations (up to 19 rows measured), so one click relabels finished siblings FAILED; the same non-uniqueness makes the detail view's unordered QueryRow return an arbitrary sibling per open. Scope the UPDATE to non-terminal rows, answer the nothing-left-to-terminate case with 409 ALREADY_TERMINAL instead of a 500, and pin the detail SELECT to root-first-oldest-first LIMIT 1 — with sqlmock tests whose SQL regexes are the contract, mutation-proven before submission.

edits.rationale: Scope the terminate UPDATE to non-terminal rows so terminating a correlation can never rewrite finished work. correlation_id is shared by parent and sub-orchestrations (up to 19 rows measured under one), so the unscoped form relabelled COMPLETED siblings as FAILED.
edits.sketch:
query := `
 		UPDATE orchestration_states
 		SET status = $2, error = $3, updated_at = NOW()
 		WHERE correlation_id = $1
+		  AND status NOT IN ('COMPLETED', 'FAILED')
 	`
 (RowsAffected()==0 -> sql.ErrNoRows retained; its meaning is now 'no non-terminal rows', which the caller distinguishes via its earlier existence lookup)

edits.rationale: With the scoped UPDATE, RowsAffected==0 on an existing correlation means everything under it is already terminal. The handler's preceding getWorkflowState call already 404s a missing correlation, so ErrNoRows here becomes 409 ALREADY_TERMINAL with a plain-language body instead of a 500 that reads as a broken endpoint.

Make the detail lookup deterministic on multi-row correlations: the root orchestration (parent_orchestration_id IS NULL) first, oldest first within that, LIMIT 1 — so the same correlation always answers the admin detail view with the same row, and the __step_error panel stops appearing and disappearing between two opens of the same item.
edits.sketch:
FROM orchestration_states
 		WHERE correlation_id = $1
+		ORDER BY (parent_orchestration_id IS NOT NULL), created_at
+		LIMIT 1

edits.rationale: Pin both contracts in the package's existing sqlmock convention (spec_update_guard_test.go). The expected-SQL regexes ARE the contract: sqlmock matches them against the issued SQL, so deleting the status filter or the ORDER BY fails the suite. Both mutations were applied and observed to fail before submission. Three tests: scoped-update happy path 200; all-rows-terminal 409 ALREADY_TERMINAL; unknown correlation 404.

plan.risks: The status filter's literal set ('COMPLETED','FAILED') must stay in step with the platform's terminal vocabulary — state.go declares exactly these two as terminal today (INITIALIZED/RUNNING/EXECUTING_STEP/AWAITING_RESPONSES are live states); a future terminal status added to state.go and not here would make terminate relabel rows that are already finished under the new name. A reviewer should check nothing else calls updateWorkflowStatus (it has one caller, the terminate arm) and that no consumer depended on terminate relabelling COMPLETED rows (none found; the behaviour was unreachable until e6350e74b). The 409 is a behaviour change for a case that previously answered 500 after relabelling finished rows — strictly an improvement, but any SPA error-matching on the old 500 text should be checked (the SPA displays err.message verbatim; no string-match found). getWorkflowState's new ORDER BY changes WHICH row multi-row correlations return (root instead of arbitrary) — the resume arm reads client_id from that row; client_id is constant within a correlation, so resume is unaffected.
